report.summary: People buy plant sensors, but few pay for a sensor alone. No direct competitor sells the music angle in the sources found. That could mean a small market or an open one.

competitors.name: Consumer soil sensors
competitors.what: Track moisture, send alerts, no sound.

competitors.name: Generative music toys
competitors.what: Playful, but not tied to a living plant.

demand_signals.text: Plant communities ask for sensors that are fun to look at, not only useful.

risks.text: Hardware cost and shipping make a small production run expensive.

next_steps: Build one working unit and show it to five plant owners.
Test whether people pay for the music or the sensor.

measures.reason: Plant sensors are common; turning them into music is not.
Water the plant and the room changes. It demos in ten seconds.
Firmware, sound, and art each get a clear piece to own.
One sensor and a synth patch fit a weekend; the enclosure may not.

cool.why: A living plant you can hear is instantly shareable. The main risk is the sound design: it has to stay pleasant for hours.

note: Sample report (demo data). Sources are placeholders.
